chunks: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another in the least, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken, and they will not be helped.

key_terms.تَجْزِي: Will suffice or be of benefit
key_terms.يَوْمًا: A Day (specifically the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What happens to intercession and ransom on the Day of Judgment according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the principle of individual accountability (mas'uliyya al-fard) while clarifying that intercession (shafa'ah) is not an independent right but solely by God's permission, often linked to the merit of the Ahl al-Bayt. It highlights the cessation of worldly compensations (adl) and the finality of divine judgment, reinforcing the theological distinction between general intercession and specific, granted intercession.
